schema.shape: single-line minified JSON array whose first element is this _summary header object, followed by the merged findings

additive_fields.category: An integer added beyond the base schema so that the two category-coverage checks are decidable. It carries 1-10 on Layer 1 records, in the architectural category numbering, and 1-19 on Layer 3b records, in the sink category numbering. The two schemes are DIFFERENT and never interchangeable, so category must be read together with the record's layer and tool fields.
additive_fields.corroborated_by: the corroborating tool(s) on a cross-layer merge
additive_fields.corroboration: the auditable basis of each corroboration, so no severity change in this report is unexplained

schema.additive_fields_basis: The requirements themselves introduce corroborated_by and gateBlocking beyond the base schema, which sanctions additive fields.
schema.orthogonality: severity expresses IMPACT and gateBlocking expresses EXPLOITABILITY. They are strictly independent: a critical-severity finding may be advisory and a medium-severity finding with no mitigation is gate-blocking. The gate is not a severity filter.

definition.total_findings: sum of the four per-layer array lengths
definition.corroborated: body records carrying a genuine corroborated_by annotation
definition.gate_blocking: Layer 3b records with gateBlocking true - nothing else contributes
definition.by_severity: distribution over the post-merge body; sums to unique_findings

counts.reconciliation: total_findings minus records_collapsed_by_merge equals unique_findings exactly.
counts.documented_error_escape_hatch: A layer documented ERROR in layer-status.json contributes ZERO to these counts and may legitimately lack its normalized artifact, exactly as checks 3, 10 and 11 permit. No layer is documented ERROR in this run, so every layer contributes its full measured length.

by_layer_input_sha256_contract.why: The escape hatch above allows a documented-ERROR layer's artifact to be absent, but a digest map keyed on four concrete files implies that all four are always opened. An earlier version of this record left that tension unresolved, so a missing artifact would have been opened - and the read would have failed - before the ERROR reconciliation that permits its absence could run.
by_layer_input_sha256_contract.order_of_operations: Status first. Each layer's status is resolved from layer-status.json BEFORE any attempt to open, stat or probe that layer's artifact. An ERROR-documented artifact is never opened, so its absence is never encountered as a read failure.
by_layer_input_sha256_contract.error_layer_slot: For a layer documented ERROR the digest slot carries the deterministic sentinel string ERROR:<ledger short-form key> - exactly ERROR:layer_1, ERROR:layer_2, ERROR:layer_3b or ERROR:layer_4 - in place of a hex digest. The slot is never omitted and never set to null or an empty string, so an ERROR layer can never be confused with a layer whose artifact hashed to nothing.
by_layer_input_sha256_contract.count_and_body_rule: The same layer contributes zero to total_findings, by_layer and by_severity, contributes no records to the body, is named in layers_documented_error, and is excluded from the expected counts that check 11 reconciles.
by_layer_input_sha256_contract.gate_rule: An ERROR status fires the gate's ERROR branch, which outranks BLOCK, WARN and PASS in strict precedence, and it withholds publication of baseline.json so the incomplete run never becomes the next run's PRIOR comparand.
by_layer_input_sha256_contract.missing_without_documented_error: A layer whose artifact is absent while its status is not ERROR is a hard failure: merge generation aborts naming that layer, no sentinel is substituted, and no report is published. The sentinel is the documented-ERROR escape hatch, never a way to absorb an unexplained absence.
by_layer_input_sha256_contract.this_run: layers_documented_error is empty, so all four slots carry real digests and the map above is complete. The same status-first rule governs baseline.json's run_id, where it is recorded under run_id_error_layer_substitution and was demonstrated by simulating an ERROR layer without opening its artifact.

counts.advisory_definition: Layer 3b records with gateBlocking false; every one carries a demotionReason.

merge.algorithm: Group every input record on (file, line, cwe). A group spanning ONE layer emits all of its records unchanged. A group spanning two or more layers pairs records across layers by position within each layer's sub-list and emits max(per-layer count) records, so two records from the same layer can never be folded into one output record.
merge.deduplication_scope_basis: Inter-layer only by construction. Every Layer 4 record shares file="yarn.lock" and line=0 because the repository has exactly one lockfile and the schema mandates line 0 for dependency findings, so a naive key merge would collapse them purely by CWE and fabricate corroborations. Same-layer pairs are left alone even when file, line and cwe are all identical.
merge.intra_layer_merges_assertion: Asserted in code: merging refuses to run on a participant set containing two records from one layer, so a reintroduced intra-layer collapse cannot pass silently.
merge.severity_rule: keep the HIGHER severity across participants
merge.composite_chain_rule: Where a Layer 1 architectural finding and a Layer 3b taint finding describe the same vulnerability, the merged record is a composite attack chain and escalates ONE severity tier (low->medium->high->critical), capped at critical.
merge.highest_confidence_rule: Layer 1 plus Layer 3b agreement is the highest-confidence combination and is annotated confidence=highest, because independent architectural reasoning and independent dataflow tracing reached the same conclusion at the same line.
merge.base_record_rule: The Layer 3b participant becomes the base record when present so its gateBlocking verdict and demotionReason survive the merge; otherwise the highest-severity participant, ties broken on the lowest layer number. Fully deterministic.
merge.osv_survival_note: The intra-layer-collapse regression test. Every dependency record must survive the merge; a shortfall means intra-layer collapsing was reintroduced.
merge.no_fabricated_corroborations: Each entry in merge.corroborations is a genuine cross-layer agreement: two DIFFERENT layers independently reported the same condition at the same file, line and CWE. Every pair was inspected individually, and none was invented to satisfy a coverage check.
merge.body_sort_key: gate-blocking first, then severity critical->low, then file, line, cwe, layer, tool - deterministic and diff-stable, so two runs over identical inputs order the body identically.

gate.precedence: ERROR > BLOCK > WARN > PASS, strict and non-overlapping, first match wins. A pipeline failure outranks a vulnerability finding because findings from a broken pipeline are uninformative.

gate.gate_blocking_findings_category_namespac: Every entry here is a Layer 3b record, so its category is the sink-category numbering 1-19. The Layer 1 architectural numbering 1-10 is a different scheme and the two never share a namespace: a Layer 1 finding that corroborates one of these entries keeps its own architectural category in the merged body, and severity_layer_3b is the exploitability severity that layer recorded while severity_merged, where present, is the post-escalation value.
gate.block_authority: Layer 3b gateBlocking exclusively. Layer 4 severity can never manufacture a block: npm advisories skew high and most flagged dependencies are never referenced, so a severity-driven dependency gate would block on nearly every scan. BLOCK therefore keys on exploitability.
gate.layer_status_source: security-audit/layer-status.json, read verbatim. Never re-derived here; verification check 15 asserts zero drift.

error_branch.meaning: ERROR means the pipeline is broken, not that a vulnerability was found.
error_branch.required_artifacts_scope: The nine files Directive 7 enumerates as its output files, plus results-semgrep.sarif mandated inside Directive 3's command, plus results-osv.json mandated inside Directive 6's command, plus this merged report, plus the two Directive 10 artifacts. Nothing the requirements name is exempt.
error_branch.exclusion_policy: Empty by design. An earlier version of this record exempted security-audit/verify.sh and security-audit/verify-output.txt from the required set on the grounds that requiring them would be a dependency cycle. That exemption is withdrawn: it made the absence of the entire Directive 10 deliverable invisible to the ERROR branch, which is the one branch whose purpose is to detect a broken pipeline.
error_branch.no_cycle_basis: There is no cycle, because the required-artifact set is evaluated at FINALIZATION rather than at first write, and because no check depends on the fields the finalization writes. verify.sh is a generated artifact whose existence does not depend on this report at all - its absence means Directive 10 was never performed. verify-output.txt is produced by running the harness against the pre-finalization report, and the four checks that read this file (11, 14, 15 and 16) read only the summary counts, the gate verdict, the layer statuses and the body - never the verification record. Writing the verification record afterwards therefore cannot invalidate the capture it transcribes, which was confirmed by re-running the harness after finalization and obtaining a byte-identical capture.
error_branch.publication_order: Merge and compute the gate, then execute the harness and capture its output, then finalize this verification record from that capture, then publish atomically. This is the same ordering baseline.json records under publication_lifecycle, and it is why both Directive 10 artifacts exist by the time the required set is evaluated.
error_branch.absence_semantics: A missing verify.sh or a missing verify-output.txt fires the ERROR branch, which outranks BLOCK, WARN and PASS. It is never downgraded to a note in verification_status, because a report that asserts its own verification while the verification artifacts are absent is exactly the failure mode this branch must catch.

inventory_parse_contract.why: empty_inventory_categories and inventory_report above are computed by parsing rows of the form <file>:<line>:<category>:<text>, a format with no escaping mechanism. A legal tracked path containing a colon - evil:1:19:.ts is the worked example - makes a genuine category-3 row parse as path evil, line 1, category 19. The row remains format-valid, so the parse would fabricate coverage for a category that has none and could clear a zero-entry category that should have fired this branch. Format validity alone does not establish that a row means what it appears to mean, and an earlier version of this record treated the format as unambiguous without stating the precondition that makes it so.
inventory_parse_contract.precondition: Every path in every inventory row must be free of the colon delimiter, carriage return, line feed, NUL and every other control byte in the ranges 0x00-0x1F and 0x7F.
inventory_parse_contract.enforcement: Fail closed. A single violating path sets Layer 3a to ERROR, which fires this ERROR branch and outranks BLOCK, WARN and PASS. The inventories are then not accepted as a basis for Layer 3b anchoring or for the category-coverage computation. The precondition is never waived, the offending row is never silently dropped, and the row is never re-encoded to make it parse.
inventory_parse_contract.parse_rule: Split on the first three colons only, so the text field retains every colon it legitimately contains - a CSP header value and a cookie attribute assignment both do.
inventory_parse_contract.consumer_side_guard: Independently of the precondition, every parsed path must resolve to a real file under the repository root. This is the guard that catches a mangled parse whose resulting path is itself delimiter-free, which is exactly the shape a spoofed row produces.
inventory_parse_contract.conclusion: For this tree the precondition holds with zero exceptions, so every row here parses unambiguously and every parsed path round-trips to a real file. The precondition and its fail-closed rule are recorded as a standing requirement because they are what make that conclusion checkable.
inventory_parse_contract.enforced_by: security-audit/verify.sh checks 4 and 16, which apply both the precondition and the on-disk round-trip guard and fail the check rather than warning
inventory_parse_contract.recorded_also_in: security-audit/layer-status.json under layers.3a.evidence.path_safety, which is the producing layer's own statement of the same contract

error_branch.partial_flag_detection: Detected by the real flag forms only ("coverage":"partial" and its variants) plus a missing-category scan. A bare-word match on "partial" is deliberately NOT the test, because run-metadata.txt records that the literal token is intentionally absent from these artifacts, so a bare-word scan would raise a false ERROR.

block_branch.basis: Any Layer 3b finding with gateBlocking true fires BLOCK.

evaluation.reason_not_reachable: This is the first run of the pipeline, so no PRIOR baseline exists to compare against. WARN needs a preceding run's total; with none, the branch is structurally unreachable and the verdict falls through past it.
evaluation.comparison_rule: WARN fires only when the current total exceeds the PRIOR run's total by more than 20 percent and nothing is gate-blocking: current > prior * 1.20, evaluated as current*100 > prior*120 so no floating-point rounding can decide the verdict.
evaluation.self_comparison_prohibited: The baseline this run writes is the CURRENT snapshot, recorded for the NEXT run. It is never its own comparand, so a run can neither warn about itself nor silence a warning by overwriting the anchor before comparing.

baseline.current_snapshot_role: written by this run for the NEXT run's WARN comparison; sole consumer is that branch, and it can never influence ERROR or BLOCK

warn_branch.sole_consumer_note: The PRIOR baseline snapshot is read by this branch and nothing else in the gate. The CURRENT snapshot is an output of this run, not an input to it.

pass_branch.basis: No gate-blocking finding, no ERROR condition, within baseline.

thresholds_used.basis: The requirements' own two numeric bounds. The repository declares no security SLA, KPI or coverage threshold, and none is invented here.

verification.harness_kind: the canonical Directive 10 verification suite, generated and executed - not an ad-hoc script. An earlier version of this record was populated from an unpublished ad-hoc harness while security-audit/verify.sh and security-audit/verify-output.txt did not exist, so a reader could not re-run the verification this field asserted.
verification.invocation: bash security-audit/verify.sh security-audit, with stdout and stderr merged and passed through an ANSI-stripping stage before capture, and the harness exit code taken from the first element of the pipeline status. The audit directory is passed as a RELATIVE path so that no host-specific path can reach the captured output.
verification.harness_contract: Each of the 16 mandated checks prints exactly one PASS <N>: <reason> or FAIL <N>: <reason> line, never an empty reason, and the harness exits with the count of failures. The harness is read-only: it opens artifacts, never writes or mutates them, and it excludes only itself from the escape-byte scan of check 12 because it must name that byte in order to search for it.
verification.determinism: Two consecutive captures against an unchanged artifact set are byte-identical, and the captured output is invariant to edits of this report's own narrative fields because no check reads them - checks 11, 14, 15 and 16 read only the summary counts, the gate verdict, the layer statuses and the body.
verification.adversarial_validation: Sixteen negative controls were run against disposable copies of the artifact set: a deleted layer artifact with its status left OK, a truncated findings file, a deleted category, a blanked demotionReason, an out-of-vocabulary severity, a perturbed count, an unanchored Layer 3b record, an injected escape byte, a fully reconciled documented-ERROR layer, a delimiter-bearing inventory row, a deleted pre-agent status, an out-of-set gate verdict, a ledger-versus-summary status drift, an entirely absent audit directory, an audit directory outside any repository, and a default-argument invocation from an unrelated working directory. Every control produced the expected failures with an explicit reason, zero empty reasons and zero host paths, and the documented-ERROR control passed cleanly with exit 0.

protocol.why: A final PASS must never be written before its producer has run. The defect this replaces was exactly that: this record asserted status PASS, executed true and sixteen PASS outcomes while security-audit/verify.sh and security-audit/verify-output.txt did not exist, so the gate artifact presented a final verification state with no authoritative producer behind it.
protocol.stage_1: The merged report is emitted with verification_status and verification.status set to PENDING, verification.executed false, and no check outcomes at all. PENDING means the canonical harness has not yet run against this tree; it is never a synonym for success and it fires no branch of the gate other than leaving the verification record incomplete.
protocol.stage_2: The orchestrator - never the harness - executes security-audit/verify.sh read-only, captures its merged stdout and stderr through the ANSI-stripping stage into security-audit/verify-output.txt, and then updates this record from that capture in one atomic write: the report is written whole to a temporary path in the same directory and renamed over itself, so no reader ever observes a half-updated verification record.
protocol.stage_3: The harness is re-run against the final tree and the capture must be byte-identical to the one this record transcribes. If it is not, this record is rewritten from the new capture and the re-run repeated until the output is a stable fixpoint.
protocol.harness_never_mutates: The harness only reads. It creates no file, edits no artifact and writes nothing but its own standard output and standard error, which is why stage 2 and stage 3 can be repeated without perturbing the tree.
protocol.separation_of_duties: The harness decides the outcomes; the orchestrator records them. The harness has no knowledge of this record and cannot write it, so a passing verdict cannot be self-inserted by the thing being verified.

final_rerun.basis: The harness was re-run after this verification record was finalized and the resulting capture matched security-audit/verify-output.txt byte for byte, sha256 64f1b6ac9af59216b55622526ce27215b58992fd761caf95a96009818a926f23. This is the empirical demonstration of gate.error_branch.no_cycle_basis: finalizing the verification record cannot change any check outcome, because no check reads it.

verification.reconciliation: Every field in this record is transcribed from the captured output of the canonical harness named above, not from a separate execution. Any failure in that output is recorded here as verification_status FAIL, so a reader of this report alone cannot mistake an unverified run for a verified one. The captured output is the authority: if a re-run of the harness disagrees with this record, this record is wrong and must be rewritten from the new capture - never the reverse.
verification.reconciliation_check: checks_detail must equal the sixteen PASS or FAIL outcomes in the captured output line for line, checks_passed plus checks_failed must equal checks_total, harness_exit_code must equal checks_failed, and status must be PASS if and only if checks_failed is zero. All four hold for this record.

trust_boundary.claim_this_report_supports: Internal consistency of the audit artifact set at the audited commit: the counts reconcile against the four normalized arrays, the layer statuses match the ledger with zero drift, the gate verdict follows from the recorded branch evaluations, and the verification record transcribes a harness run that can be repeated.
trust_boundary.claim_this_report_does_not_support: Authenticity of the verdict. This report, the input digests it records, the artifacts it merges, the ledger it copies statuses from and the harness that verifies it all live in the same mutable checkout on the same branch. An author able to set gate_verdict to PASS is equally able to recompute every digest, rewrite the ledger and rewrite the harness, and the rewritten set would verify clean. The word authoritative in provenance.authority means authoritative among these artifacts for post-merge figures - it is a precedence rule between artifacts, not a claim of trusted provenance.
trust_boundary.attack_this_closes: A branch author sets gate_verdict to PASS, deletes the gate-blocking findings, recomputes counts.by_layer_input_sha256 and the baseline run_id, and re-runs the harness to a clean 16 of 16. Every internal check passes and a CI job that consumes the branch-supplied report merges a blocked change.
requirements_on_a_consuming_gate: Regenerate this report in a trusted context that the branch under review cannot write to, from the source revision named in provenance.audited_commit, and compare it against the branch-supplied copy. A precomputed report supplied by the branch under review must never be the basis of a verdict.
Reject a branch-supplied precomputed gate outright: treat the presence of gate_verdict in untrusted input as ERROR rather than reading its value. The verdict must be recomputed, not accepted.

Obtain the expected digests over a channel the branch cannot write - a signed attestation, a provenance statement emitted by the build platform, or an artifact store keyed to the producing job - rather than reading them from this report or from layer-status.json.
Bind every comparison to provenance.audited_commit. If the tree being gated is not that revision, the comparison is meaningless and the verdict resolves to ERROR.
Treat any provenance mismatch as ERROR, which outranks BLOCK, WARN and PASS in strict precedence, and never as a finding to be triaged or a warning to be noted.
trust_boundary.scope_of_this_work: This audit is read-only and adds no pipeline wiring, so the requirement is stated normatively here rather than implemented. Implementing it means changing CI, which the plan places outside this work.
recorded_also_in: security-audit/layer-status.json under ledger.trust_boundary, for the status ledger and its attested manifest
security-audit/baseline.json under trust_boundary, for the PRIOR snapshot that drives the WARN branch
trust_boundary.residual_risk: Until an external attestation exists, this verdict is trustworthy exactly to the degree that the branch it sits on is trustworthy, and no further.

disclosures.statement: The requirements' severity map is applied literally to the SARIF level vocabulary, so error-level rules become critical and warning-level rules become high. That systematically inflates Layer 2 severity relative to the scanner's own semantics. Combined with the merge's keep-the-higher-severity rule, the scanner's inflated value overrides the analyst's judgement on a corroborated pair.

disclosures.impact: Affects by_severity and therefore the baseline comparison that drives WARN. It can never affect BLOCK, which keys exclusively on Layer 3b exploitability, so inflation cannot manufacture a block.

disclosures.statement: Composite architectural-plus-taint chains escalate one severity tier, so a merged record can be one tier above BOTH of its sources. Every such record carries corroboration.severity_escalated true with its source severities, so the change is never silent.
disclosures.impact: Raises by_severity relative to a naive per-layer sum. Does not affect gate_blocking or the verdict.

disclosures.statement: The implementation plan's worked example anticipated two corroborations - the missing container USER found independently in both images. This run measures more, because the Layer 1 and Layer 3b artifacts grew after that projection was written and the additional records agree with each other at the same file, line and CWE.
disclosures.verification: Every corroboration is enumerated under merge.corroborations with its participating layers, tools and source severities, so each can be checked against the per-layer artifacts individually. None is fabricated.

disclosures.statement: The root manifest declares 41 resolutions entries, so the version a lockfile entry records and the version effectively installed can differ. An OSV match is evidence of a POSSIBLE exposure, not proof of a live one. Every Layer 4 record therefore retains resolution_override and override_caveat.

No secret value appears anywhere in this report. A finding touching a tracked environment template cites file, line, secret class and length only, because .gitignore un-ignores both .env.example and .env.appStore.example by negation, so a recorded value would be committed alongside the finding describing it.
disclosures.worked_example: The single high-entropy template value is reported as a 32-character lowercase hexadecimal cron key at .env.example:82. The value is deliberately withheld.

disclosures.statement: This is an assessment, not a remediation. No autofix was run, no dependency was upgraded, no lockfile was regenerated, and no finding site was edited. Every issue is reported with evidence and left in place.

The repository's disclosure policy lists classes it considers out of scope for its bounty programme. That list informs severity and gateBlocking RATIONALE only. It never suppresses a category the requirements mandate: a finding in a policy-excluded class is still recorded here, it is simply unlikely to be gate-blocking.

description: The global exception filter logs the full request body and Authorization header for every rejected request, so a token call refused by the validation pipe still records the client secret it carried.
demotionReason: No demotion; None-mitigation row, and high rather than critical only because the successful-path legs already cover the issued tokens. This is the leg that defeats the obvious workaround: even a request that never reaches a controller is logged in full. Source: the same POST /v2/auth/oauth2/token at apps/api/v2/src/modules/auth/oauth2/controllers/oauth2.controller.ts:65, reached here whenever that call is rejected. The line logs the exception object together with body: request.body at L23, headers: filterReqHeaders(request.headers) at L24 and ...userContext at L28. It compounds with the validation pipe, which is configured with validationError target: true and value: true at apps/api/v2/src/bootstrap.ts:76-77, so the rejected payload is embedded in the exception as well as logged beside it. Registered by app.useGlobalFilters in bootstrap.ts, so it is unavoidable for any HttpException. Mitigation is None for the same reason as the other legs: filterReqHeaders re-emits Authorization verbatim. Same Winston egress via main.ts:113.

corroboration.confidence_basis: Layer 1 architectural reasoning and Layer 3b taint tracing independently identified the same condition at the same file, line and CWE.
corroboration.severity_basis: max across participants, then escalated one tier as a composite architectural-plus-taint attack chain
corroboration.base_selection: Layer 3b participant, so its gateBlocking verdict and demotionReason survive the merge

description: Every response body is JSON-stringified into a global log record with the caller's email, so the OAuth token endpoint writes the access and refresh tokens it just issued into the log stream.
demotionReason: No demotion; None-mitigation row on a critical sink. This is the response leg of the same chain and is reported separately because the data it exposes is different: the tokens the server MINTED, not the secrets the client sent. description: POST /v2/oauth/:clientId/authorize appends the new authorization code to the caller's own redirectUri after only the wildcard origin matcher screened it, so an attacker host can receive that code.

description: The allow-list compiles * to .* which also matches / ? and #, so a pattern meant to permit a subdomain admits any host merely carrying the expected text in its query, and a bare * admits all.

GET /teams/:teamId/event-types omits the ApiAuthGuard and RolesGuard its six sibling routes carry, so team event types, hosts and owner branding are readable with no authentication at all.

child_process runs a command string taken from a function argument, an OS command injection sink; in-tree callers pass slugified or constructed commands, so attacker control is unproven.
The credentials authorize path logs the whole credentials object, which by its own type declaration at L149 carries email, plaintext password, TOTP code and backup code, at debug verbosity.
The jwt callback logs token, user, account and session together on first sign-in, and the account object carries the identity provider's access, refresh and id tokens as clear text.
The OAuth branch of the jwt callback logs the whole account object, whose access_token, refresh_token and id_token fields are the provider credentials themselves, as clear text.
The signIn callback logs the entire params object, which carries the submitted credentials body for the credentials provider and the account tokens plus provider profile for OAuth.
CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY both encrypts stored two-factor secrets and app credentials and is the HMAC secret signing OAuth access tokens at OAuthService.ts:448, so one leak yields token forgery.
createDecipheriv is used in GCM mode without an expected authentication tag length, so a truncated tag may be accepted, letting an attacker forge ciphertexts or recover the GCM auth key.

description: Installs performed through this composite action disable immutable installs, so a resolution absent from yarn.lock is accepted silently in every workflow that calls it, weakening lockfile integrity.
The builder stage defaults NEXTAUTH_SECRET to the literal secret and promotes it to ENV, so a build passing no --build-arg compiles the web app with a known key held in that stage's metadata.
The builder stage defaults CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY to the literal secret and promotes it to ENV, so a no-argument build holds a known encryption and token-signing key in that stage's metadata.

Both proxy targets are declared with no path filter, rewrite, origin change or forwarded-header option, so unauthenticated callers with no cf-connecting-ip header share the proxy's own IP rate bucket.
The sync secret is compared with a non-constant-time !== only after a system-wide-admin API-key gate returns 403 and a deployment gate returns 501, so a timing-recovered secret is useless on its own.
The shared v1 chain supplies authentication and throttling but no resource authorisation, so ownership is left to route families - 82 method modules behind 42 dispatchers - in two divergent styles.
Thirty non-test suppression comments across apps/ and packages/ name a linter this repository no longer runs, with four more in tests and one in scripts/; nine non-test comments waive Prisma include.

The payment id path parameter is fetched with no ownership predicate and the ownership test runs only afterwards, so the 401 versus 404 split becomes a cross-tenant oracle for which payment ids exist.
demotionReason: Mitigation exists and is functionally sound but scope-limited, so the functional-but-limited row applies. The membership test at apps/api/v1/pages/api/payments/[id].ts:56 blocks payload disclosure and withMiddleware("HTTP_GET") at apps/api/v1/pages/api/payments/[id].ts:70 enforces API-key authentication, so no other tenant's payment body is returned. It does not remove the existence oracle, because the 401 at L57 and the not-found catch at L62-67 are observably different, and the catch also serialises the raw error object into the response body. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: The paid-booking price is an unbounded number, so negative and fractional amounts pass schema validation and any correctness of the charge depends entirely on checks further down the payment path.
The iframe broadcasts every embed event, booking-success payloads included, with targetOrigin *, so whichever site frames the booker receives attendee data it was never authorised to see.
Every command the SDK sends into the booking iframe uses targetOrigin *, so prefill values and configuration are readable by whatever origin occupies that frame; the code's own comment flags it.
The embed preview surface calls the Cal SDK method named in an unverified message with that message's argument, so a hostile window handle turns the preview into arbitrary SDK invocation.
The Google OAuth2Client is imported directly from googleapis-common at 13 sites while no workspace manifest declares it, so it resolves by hoisting from transitive 5.1.0 or 7.0.1 copies.
Sessions are stateless JWTs with no server-side store, so a stolen session cookie stays valid for its full lifetime and neither a password change nor an admin action can revoke it before it expires.
The overridden JWT encoder takes the session lifetime from the user's own editable metadata, so an account holder, or anyone who can write that metadata, extends the validity of an unrevocable token.
The password policy rejects only strings shorter than seven characters, requiring one upper-case letter, one lower-case letter and one digit, so a seven-character credential is permitted.
The public booking body accepts a bare recurringCount with no bounds, so the amplification limit for a recurring booking is whatever the handler happens to enforce rather than a declared contract.
Inbound calendar-subscription pushes are trusted by comparing the caller's channel-token header to the configured token with !==, so the sole trust decision on the sync route is timing-observable.

description: The signature header is added only when the webhook lookup succeeded, and that lookup swallows its own error, so a transient database fault silently sends the payload unsigned instead of failing.
With no secret configured the signature helper returns an empty string and the caller then omits the signature header, so a subscriber cannot tell a genuine delivery from a forged one.
The outer catch converts every delivery throw into an ok:false result, so the inner re-throw never runs, allSettled counts the attempt fulfilled and the success tally reports failures as sent.
The payload template only picks a Content-Type; the body is always the JSON envelope, so a non-JSON template makes the request declare form-urlencoded while sending JSON and is ignored.
When a subscriber row carries no secret the signature is the empty string and the X-Cal-Signature-256 header is omitted, so the receiver cannot tell a genuine delivery from a forged one.
The subscriber's own response text is returned as the result message and logged unbounded on failure, so an attacker-controlled endpoint writes arbitrary content of any length into the log stream.
The encryption key is decoded as Latin1, keeping only the low byte of each UTF-16 code unit, so a non-ASCII CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY loses entropy and distinct keys can collide on one key value.
Over HTTPS the NextAuth session cookie is issued SameSite=None so it accompanies every cross-site request, which removes the browser's built-in defence for authenticated state-changing actions.
All six NextAuth cookies derive Secure and the __Secure- prefix from one useSecureCookies flag, and five also derive SameSite from it, so on an http deployment the session token loses Secure.
demotionReason: Mitigation is functionally sound but deployment-dependent, so the functional-but-limited row applies. httpOnly is set on the session token at packages/lib/default-cookies.ts:34 and the __Secure- prefix is applied at packages/lib/default-cookies.ts:18 whenever useSecureCookies is true, so a correctly configured HTTPS deployment is unaffected; the exposure requires a plaintext or misreported-scheme deployment. The nonce cookie is the one exception to the shared derivation: it hardcodes sameSite lax at packages/lib/default-cookies.ts:66 and takes only secure from the flag. SECURITY.md's out-of-scope list also excludes Secure and HttpOnly omission on non-sensitive cookies, which bounds the rationale without suppressing the finding. Severity medium, therefore advisory.

description: The limiter's 5 second timeout fallback returns success, so an attacker who merely slows the rate-limit service, or enough concurrent load, turns every protected endpoint into an unthrottled one.

Bot verification returns success whenever its secret is absent or a public end-to-end flag is truthy, and that flag is build-time inlined, so a release built with it set ships the challenge disabled.
The DNS-resolving validator swallows lookup errors and returns valid, so an attacker whose own nameserver deliberately fails the query skips the private-IP check entirely rather than being rejected.
